name: LAPS Reader
description: LAPS Reader is a Windows PowerShell/WPF GUI tool that retrieves Windows LAPS passwords stored in Intune (Entra) via Microsoft Graph. It signs in to Graph, resolves a device by display name, and displays the local account, password, backup time, and account SID with a one-click copy. Intended for IT/helpdesk staff, it requires the Microsoft.Graph.Authentication module and permissions DeviceLocalCredential.Read.All and Device.Read.All.
author: Reshat Bekteshi

securityCheck.aiSummary: Overall assessment: The code implements a legitimate Intune/LAPS admin tool with Graph API usage and proper authentication flow. The primary security concern is credential exposure: the tool reads and presents LAPS passwords to an authenticated admin and allows copying to clipboard, which elevates the risk surface if RBAC or device security is weak. The only notable ancillary risk is the on-demand installation of the Microsoft Graph Authentication module from PSGallery, which could be mitigated by bundling/signing dependencies or enforcing trusted sources. No hardcoded secrets or external data exfiltration appear, and there are no malicious patterns beyond the expected credential access for LAPS. Recommend tightening RBAC, minimizing in-memory credential handling, avoiding unnecessary clipboard exposure, and ensuring module installation is restricted to trusted sources with signature verification.
